summary: Somerset County, ME tower on Mount Kineo, built 1917 as a 64-ft steel lookout; cab gone, now a public viewing platform in Mount Kineo State Park.

facts.status_note: Structure stands with the cab no longer in place (FFLA asterisk legend); now a viewing platform

access.note: Mount Kineo State Park, 800 acres, established 1990; no road access to the park; trails from the park entrance. Article also says accessible by water only.

visit.trail_note: Carriage Trail from the park entrance, with the Bridle Trail and Indian Trail; the Bridle Trail runs 0.4 mile to the summit observation tower

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give 40 ft (June 1917 newspaper), about 65 ft (1917 state report) and 64 ft (1917 annual report, 1920 inventory, 2021 article). The record's 19.5 m equals 64 ft, which is the majority figure and the most recent; the 40 and 65 ft figures are noted but not used in facts.

The article says accessible by water only, yet also says a narrow strip of land connects the peninsula to the mainland and there is no road access to the park. Recorded as no road access; trails from the park entrance.

The 1918 newspaper calls the station federal; the Forest Lookouts history lists the Maine Forestry District. Recorded as Maine Forestry District per the lookout history; the federal label is unresolved.

notes_for_editor: Dates for cab removal and the viewing-platform conversion were not found in the pages read, so no events are recorded for them. The 1960s end of use comes from the Maine Trail Finder story alone and has no exact year, so it is not an event. Search snippets (not read as pages) said the tower was used until about 1960 and mentioned the cab; not used. Maine Trail Finder title checked against the page and corrected to Above the Trees - 5 Maine Fire Tower Hikes. The Wikipedia cache for Mount Kineo had no tower matches. The OpenStreetMap node was not read. Brief height_m 19.5 is supported (64 ft); brief status and agency are supported; no corrections proposed.
